prize_parts.citation: For the theoretical prediction of flat bands at a magic twist angle in twisted bilayer graphene and the experimental discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states in moire flat-band matter.

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: B041 with MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero and Bistritzer. The round-1 exchange sharpened why. B041 is the only shortlisted case in which a quantitative theoretical prediction (flat bands at a magic angle, 2011) was followed by an experimental discovery at that angle (2018) and then by broad independent replication in twisted multilayers and other moire systems. The citation I propose is deliberately split into a theory clause and an experiment clause, so that it does not imply that the group leader alone made the observation. It credits a discovery, not a leadership role. The flat-band and correlated-insulator result is robust whatever the pairing mechanism proves to be, which answers the maturity worry as it applies to the discovery itself.
statement.case_against: I take the chair's question seriously. The unsettled pairing mechanism does not undermine the discovery of correlated states at the magic angle, but the absence of Cao and of the hBN-device groups (Dean and others) from the credited names is a real fairness problem that a three-person limit cannot repair. Eight years is also short, and a committee that waits would lose little. If the committee considers the attribution gap decisive, B001 is the more settled alternative, although its own five-to-three cut (Cirac, Zoller, Esslinger, Bloch, Greiner) is not cleaner. I also admit that no ballot has more than two explicit supporters, so my preference should not be mistaken for a consensus position.

responses.point: Danielsson prefers B020 (Gianotti, Della Negra, Jenni), crediting conception and leadership of ATLAS and CMS, but concedes that leadership roles are not scientific authorship and that the choice among four names is partly arbitrary.
responses.response: His concession is the point that decides it for me. The chair asks for a principled rule that picks three of four and still names two collaborations. I cannot construct one that does not choose between Virdee and Gianotti by convention rather than by scientific contribution. The Higgs science is overwhelming and outside my subfield, so I defer to him on its maturity. But a rule of leadership at conception or announcement would be a different kind of award from the one B041 offers, where the discovery itself maps onto named people. I regard that as a real difference in deliverability, not a ranking of importance.

responses.point: Mehlig prefers B001 (Bloch, Greiner, Esslinger, experimental only) as the mature, clean platform for Hubbard physics, and regards the unsettled pairing mechanism in B041 as an argument for a modest wait.
responses.response: I agree that B001 is the most mature of the matter-physics cases and the one I would move to if the committee decides to wait on B041. Our remaining difference is the bar. He uses the settled mechanism as a test of maturity, whereas I use independent replication of the central claim, which B041 already has. His experiment-only trio also leaves out the theoretical origin of the optical-lattice Hubbard simulator, which is a cut as consequential as mine. I do not claim it is cleaner than the B041 cut.

responses.point: Johansson moved to B001 with Bloch, Greiner and Zoller, a mixed theory and experiment prize, and notes that Jaksch is missing and that quantum advantage has not been shown.
responses.response: His mixed B001 trio has the same structure as mine, theory plus experiment, and I welcome that. The cost is exactly the one he names: the theory origin of the lattice Hubbard proposal is Jaksch and Zoller, and Cirac sits in B011, so crediting Zoller alone cannot be defended by tracing a single idea. B041 has a tighter link between the named theorists and the observed effect. I accept his point that B001 has the longer record, and his case is the strongest alternative to mine, but I do not see its attribution as easier.

responses.point: Olsson also prefers B041, and regards the missing early-career experimentalists as defensible if the citation is built around the discovery.
responses.response: The chair asked the two of us whether the citation can credit the discovery without implying the group leader alone made it. I think it can, if the prediction and the observation appear as separate clauses and the words refer to the discovery of the states and not to a laboratory. I am still more cautious than she is on the gap itself. Even with that citation, Cao and Dean are omitted, and I would not call that fully defensible. I think it is acceptable only because the three-person limit forces a cut, and only if the committee records the omission in the background text.

responses.point: Kroll moved to B013 (Katori and Ye) as the cleanest two-name credit, while noting it may be read as precision metrology and may be better timed with the redefinition of the second.
responses.response: B013 is the cleanest on attribution, and I concede that clearly. I rank it second alternative because it is also the cleanest of the three. My hesitation is the one he states himself: it builds on the 2005 comb and 2012 single-ion prizes and may be read as an advance in measurement. The matter is outside my field, so I weigh his judgement of the science more than my own. I would accept it as a prize that has a clear answer to the chair's attribution question, but I do not think clean credit alone should decide the ranking when the discovery content differs.

uncertainties: Whether the committee treats the unresolved pairing mechanism as disqualifying for now or as an open question within a durable field. I judge the latter but cannot prove it.
Whether the omission of Cao and the hBN device groups can be softened by the citation wording and background text, or remains a decisive weakness.
Whether a 2026 award would be seen as overlapping with the 2016 topological-phases prize. I judge this weak.
My assessment of the particle-physics, cold-atom and clock candidates rests on general knowledge, not specialist expertise.
statement.conflict_note: No change to my round-1 disclosure. I have no documented personal or institutional connection to any credited person in B041, B001 or B013. My general interest in correlated-electron physics and electronic-structure theory is a scientific bias I disclose, not a personal connection.
